seoTitle: How to Create an Image Slider in Shopify Dawn Theme
metaDescription: Add and customize an image slider or carousel in the Shopify Dawn theme without coding to make your store more engaging.
intro: A homepage that opens with a static single image feels flat compared to one that rotates through a few strong visuals. An image slider gives you room to introduce a new collection, promote a sale, and showcase your bestseller all in the same slot above the fold, without asking the visitor to scroll first. The Dawn theme doesn't ship a slideshow that's ready to go out of the box in every store setup, so most store owners end up adding the slider through a page builder tucked into their Shopify admin rather than a raw theme setting. This guide follows that real path end to end: opening the admin, finding the builder, adding a slider section, and configuring the slides so they look right on both desktop and mobile.

steps.heading: Start from your Shopify admin home
steps.body: Log in to your store and land on the admin Home screen, where the left sidebar lists Home, Orders, Products, Customers, Marketing, and the rest of the core sections, with your Sales channels and any installed apps grouped further down. The Home screen also surfaces a sessions-and-sales chart and a couple of suggested next steps, like activating social sign-in, which are unrelated to the slider but worth glancing at while you're here. The slider itself isn't a setting on this screen; it lives inside whatever tool builds your storefront pages, so the next step is finding that.

image.caption: The Shopify admin Home screen, with sales data up top and the full sidebar of sections and installed apps on the left.

steps.heading: Open your page builder app
steps.body: If your store uses a visual page builder app (a common approach for adding sliders, since it gives you more layout control than the bare theme editor), you'll find it listed under Apps in the sidebar. Opening it drops you into a template manager, typically showing a list of page types, home page, product, collections, blog posts, and so on, each with its own editable template. This is where you decide whether you're editing the existing home page template or building a fresh one, and it's also where you'll come back to duplicate or restore a version if a later edit goes wrong.

image.caption: The page builder app's template list, showing the store's page types with the default home page template highlighted.

steps.heading: Add and configure the slider section
steps.body: From inside the template editor, add a slider section to the layout, usually from a section or elements panel, and drop it wherever you want it on the page. Once it's placed, the section's settings panel opens on the right with a Slides list; a fresh slider typically starts with two or three placeholder slides and an "Add new slide" button so you can add more. Click into each slide to set its image, headline text, and button link individually. The same panel usually has content-width and vertical-alignment controls, which decide how much of the screen the slider fills and whether the text sits at the top, middle, or bottom of each slide.

image.caption: A slider section open for editing, with its Slides list on the right and options to add new slides or adjust content width and alignment.

steps.heading: Upload and arrange your images
steps.body: For each slide, upload a banner-sized image rather than a product thumbnail; something close to 1600 by 600 pixels avoids stretching or heavy cropping on wide monitors. Keep the images visually consistent in tone and color so the slider doesn't feel jarring as it transitions, and put your strongest image first since that's what loads before the slider even starts moving. Drag slides up or down in the list to reorder them, and delete any placeholder slide you don't end up using so it doesn't show up blank in the published slider.

steps.heading: Fine-tune the transition and timing
steps.body: Look for autoplay and transition settings, usually a toggle for autoplay, a delay in seconds, and a choice between a slide or fade transition. Three to five seconds per slide is a reasonable default: fast enough that visitors see the whole rotation without waiting, slow enough that nobody misses a slide mid-read. If your slides carry a call-to-action button, disable autoplay or extend the delay, since a slider that moves on before someone finishes reading the offer defeats the point of putting it there.

steps.heading: Preview on mobile before you publish
steps.body: Switch the editor's preview to mobile width and check every slide again; text that fits comfortably on desktop often gets cramped or overlaps the image on a phone screen, and it's common to find a headline that needs shortening or a button that needs repositioning. Confirm the slider still loads quickly on mobile too, since a heavy, unoptimized image can slow the whole homepage down on a cellular connection. Once it looks right in both views, save and publish the template so the slider goes live on your actual store.

faq.question: Do I need to edit code to add a slider in Dawn theme?
faq.answer: No. Most stores add a slider through a visual page builder app or the theme customizer's section library, both of which are point-and-click, so no code editing is required.

faq.question: How many images can I add to the slider?
faq.answer: Slider sections generally support as many slides as you want to add, with an "Add new slide" control in the settings panel, so you can start with two or three and grow the rotation later.

faq.question: Can I link each slide to a different page?
faq.answer: Yes. Each slide typically has its own button or click-through link, so you can send one slide to a collection page and another to a specific product or sale.

faq.question: Will the slider work well on mobile devices?
faq.answer: It should, but always check it yourself in the editor's mobile preview before publishing. Text and buttons that look fine on desktop sometimes need resizing to sit correctly on a small screen.
